newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lebed sees Russian presidential election this year.
newsitem.headline: Lebed sees Russian presidential election this year.

text.p: Retired general Alexander Lebed, seen by many as a possible future Russian president, told a German newspaper he believed that Boris Yeltsin's poor health would make a fresh presidential election necessary this year.
Lebed told the Berlin daily Tagesspiegel, according to an interview released ahead of publication on Tuesday, that he expected an election to be announced as early as March.

Since Yeltsin was admitted to hospital last week with pneumonia only two months after a quintuple heart bypass operation, the 46-year-old Lebed has become more and more outspoken in his demands for Yeltsin to step down.

Lebed, who came a strong third behind Yeltsin and communist Gennady Zyuganov in a presidential election last June and was then briefly made Yeltsin's security adviser, makes no secret of the fact he fancies his chances if a new election is held.
Lebed was quoted as saying he thought an election would be called in March because that was the time when Russia's recurrent crises have usually come to a head in the past.
He said he planned at that time to hold the founding congress of the Russian Republican People's Party which he is putting together to help him achieve his goals.

Lebed said he could imagine getting support from the political movements of eye surgeon Svyatoslav Fyodorov and economic reformer Grigory Yavlinsky as well as some factions of the right-wing Liberal-Democratic party under maverick leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky.
Lebed was due to meet industrialists and politicians from all major parties including Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber during a five-day visit to Germany starting on Tuesday.
